## 2. The deterministic baseline, recorded before any AI formation

This is the reference point later comparisons must be measured against. Same conversation, same evidence (`dda8a2c0…`), 57 turns, 1,000 tokens, 32 rollovers.

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Records created | 7 |
| Active / superseded | 6 / 1 |
| Captured by rule | `trained_by` 1, `ledger` 2, `code` 1, `served` 1, `never` 1, `preference` 1 |
| Duplicates suppressed | 2 |
| Corrections applied | 1 |
| Rejected for low confidence | 0 |
| Lexical recall on matched phrasing | pass (A03) |
| Lexical recall on paraphrase | **fail — abstains on "who was your trainer"** |

That last row is the deliverable of this gate as much as the passes are: it is a measured limitation of the system as built, and it names the next component.

## 3. What Gate A proves, and what it does not

**Proven:** evidence is preserved and addressable; deterministic formation produces provable records; duplicates do not accumulate; corrections supersede while preserving history; ownership is enforced at retrieval; abstention happens; assembly renders provenance.

**Not proven, and not claimed:**

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| The window manager removes evidence and records survive that removal | **Proven (simulated)** |
| KoboldCpp requests experience the same displacement | **Unproven — Gate C integration test** |
| Real token counts behave as the simulated ones | **Unproven — calibration** |
| Semantic retrieval / fusion / rerank | **Absent — Gate B** |
| AI-assisted formation | **Absent** |
| Any result about model behaviour | **None — no model has run** |

## 4. Constraints carried forward

Recorded because they are easy to violate later:

1. **Simulated rollover is not KoboldCpp rollover.** A Gate A pass says the Python window removes spans. It says nothing about what the server receives. Only an instrumented request can establish that, and it has not happened.
2. **Deterministic formation is not the final architecture.** `Q-MF-01` remains open. The adopted direction has the model propose content while the application decides placement; the deterministic path is the guarantee, not the replacement.
3. **The baseline must stay fixed while Gate B is built.** Formation is held constant so that any change in retrieval results is attributable to retrieval alone.

## 5. Gate B — definition of done, in advance

Written before the work so it cannot be defined after seeing results:

1. A semantic branch that is genuinely present, not a keyword fallback wearing its name — and it says so when its index is degraded.
2. Every hit records **which branch produced it**; a branch that never fires must be visibly dead, not indistinguishable from one that works.
3. Fusion and reranking implemented, with per-candidate scores from both branches.
4. The paraphrase probe (`"Who was your trainer, again?"`) retrieves `trained_by` — the concrete regression this gate exists to fix.
5. No regression on A01–A14, especially A08–A10 (isolation) and A11 (abstention).
6. `branches_used` never claims a branch that contributed nothing.
7. Gate A receipt re-emitted, and a Gate B receipt added; a Gate A result is never reported as a Gate B result.

## 6. Claim ceiling

Gate A passes in a simulated window with no model, no embedding model, and no server. It establishes that the pipeline exists and behaves as specified under those conditions. It establishes nothing about any language model, about real context displacement, or about the effectiveness of the architecture in use.
